learning_objective: 🎯 Understand how newly independent India chose a 'Mixed Economy' model, established Five Year Plans, and launched the Green Revolution to feed its booming population!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: After independence, everyone agreed the government must lead economic development to ensure justice and eliminate poverty. The Planning Commission was set up in 1950 to draft 'Five Year Plans' (inspired by the USSR).

India rejected both pure capitalism (USA) and pure communism (USSR). Instead, it adopted a Mixed Economy where critical industries (heavy machinery, electricity) were controlled by the state (public sector), while farming and retail remained private.

main_concepts.concept_title: 🚜 First vs. Second Five Year Plan
main_concepts.simple_explanation: The 1st Plan (1951) focused on patience, agriculture, and dams (like Bhakra Nangal) to recover from partition. The 2nd Plan (1956), drafted by P.C. Mahalanobis, rapidly shifted focus to heavy industries and rapid structural transformation.

Major debates dominated early development: Should India focus more on Agriculture (to feed people) or Industry (to become modern)? Should the Public Sector (government) or Private Sector lead the economy?

Facing massive food shortages in the 1960s, the government introduced High-Yielding Variety (HYV) seeds, fertilizers, and irrigation to rich farmers in Punjab, Haryana, and Western UP, dramatically boosting wheat production but increasing inequality.

fun_activity.title: 🏭 The Mayor's Dilemma
fun_activity.instructions: You have an empty plot of land and a limited budget. Do you build a massive dam to help farmers irrigate their crops, or a steel factory to create urban jobs and machinery? Write down your choice and one reason why it's the better option for long-term growth!

exam_tips: 📌 Understand the Bombay Plan (1944) — even private industrialists wanted the state to take a major role in heavy investments post-independence.
📌 P.C. Mahalanobis is a crucial name. He was the architect of the Second Five Year Plan focusing on rapid industrialization.
📌 When discussing the Green Revolution, always mention its dual impact: it made India self-sufficient in food, but widened the gap between rich and poor farmers.
quick_recap: ⭐ The Planning Commission was a non-constitutional body chaired by the Prime Minister.
⭐ The First Five Year Plan prioritized agriculture and poverty alleviation.
⭐ The Green Revolution primarily benefited regions with good irrigation facilities, like Punjab and Haryana, and focused largely on wheat.
